reviews.title: Kind of scammer
reviews.text:
Nebula is extremely misleading and, in my experience, charged me £49.99 after advertising a £1 payment.

At checkout, it clearly showed an option to pay £1 with Apple Pay. I paid the £1 through Apple Pay, and there was absolutely no clear indication that I was signing up for a £49.99 subscription.

Afterwards, I checked my Apple subscriptions because I wanted to make sure I hadn’t accidentally subscribed. Nebula was NOT listed there, so I had no reason to believe I had agreed to any subscription.

Then I discovered that Nebula had charged me £49.99 anyway.

How is this acceptable? If the £1 payment automatically enrolls customers into a £49.99 subscription, that needs to be made extremely clear BEFORE taking the payment — not hidden behind a £1 trial.

This feels deliberately misleading. Advertising £1 and then taking £49.99 without making the subscription terms clear is completely unacceptable.

I want my £49.99 refunded.

reviews.title: Scam beware
reviews.text:
I authorised a £1 Apple Pay purchase on 7 September. I did not knowingly agree to a separate £14.99 charge that day or a £49.99 recurring subscription charge on 14 September.

I have contacted AskNebula asking them to cancel any subscription, stop further charges, refund the money and provide evidence of exactly where the £14.99 and £49.99 charges were clearly disclosed and agreed to before I authorised Apple Pay.

In my experience, the charging structure was not clear enough and I would strongly advise anyone using the app to check the payment terms very carefully before proceeding. They take money and do not let you know - beware it’s a scam. I’ve reported to Apple too.

reviews.title: I expected answers not judgmental
reviews.text:
I’m very disappointed with this app. Some of the people on here are genuinely nice and helpful, but unfortunately, some are not.

One of my biggest issues happened when my account somehow got deleted. When I tried logging back in with the same information, it created a whole new account. Then I was questioned about why I supposedly had “a whole bunch of accounts.” I didn’t intentionally create multiple accounts—my original account was deleted, and trying to log back in created another one.

I was also criticized for asking the same or similar questions. Sometimes people repeat a question because they’re desperate for clarity, reassurance, or a better understanding of what they’re going through. That doesn’t mean they should be judged or treated badly.

After my experience, I personally don’t feel like this app is worth spending money on when you’re looking for answers. I’ve spent time on here hoping for genuine guidance, and instead I’ve walked away feeling disappointed and questioning whether the service is trustworthy.

At this point, I would rather go somewhere in person, such as Cassadaga, and speak with someone face-to-face. In my experience there, you don’t necessarily have to keep asking question after question—they can simply tell you what they feel or pick up on.

This is just my personal experience and opinion, but I feel like I wasted my time and money on this app. I expected a much better experience, and unfortunately, I’m leaving very disappointed.

Besides this very deceptive and scammy marketing technique, I found my reading very confusing and it seemed like i was just being told - this is how to read your own palm and what it means even though it supposedly scanned my palm for me - what is the point in paying for a palm reading if I’m doing it myself with your generic guide? The whole app is also run by AI so if that is important to you avoid this app. I’ve seen numerous people who had the same problem woth being charged a monthly sub after the £1 charge so don’t get caught in the same issue friends!
